key_facts: SQL is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation.

SQL is divided into three sub-languages: DDL (Data Definition Language with CREATE/ALTER/DROP), DML (Data Manipulation Language with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), and DCL (Data Control Language with COMMIT/ROLLBACK/GRANT/REVOKE).
A schema in SQL is a group of tables and other constructs that belong to the same database application, created via 'CREATE SCHEMA Schema_Name AUTHORIZATION Authorization_Identifier'.
A catalog in SQL is a named collection of schemas.
CREATE TABLE supports column constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, DEFAULT, CHECK) and table-level constraints including FOREIGN KEY with referential actions ON UPDATE and ON DELETE.
generated_text: Introduction to Structured Query Language (SQL) Structured Query Language (SQL) is a standard computer language for relational database management and data manipulation. It provides a way to define, query, modify, and control the data within a relational database. SQL commands are broadly categorized into three main sub-languages, each serving a distinct purpose: Data Definition Language (DDL) Data Manipulation Language (DML) Data Control Language (DCL) The Three Core SQL Sub-Languages Let's explore each of these categories to understand their roles in managing a database. 1. Data Definition Language (DDL) DDL commands are used to define and manage the structure of your database and its objects. DDL permits the specification of data types, structures, and any data constraints. These specifications are then stored directly in the database. The primary DDL commands are: CREATE: Used to make a new database object, such as a database, table, index, or user. ALTER: Used to modify the structure of an existing database object. DROP: Used to destroy an existing database object. 2. Data Manipulation Language (DML) DML commands are used to manage the actual data within the database tables. These commands allow you to retrieve, add, modify, and remove data. The primary DML commands are: SELECT: Used to retrieve information from a database. INSERT: Used to add one or more new tuples (rows) to a relation (table). UPDATE: Used to modify the attribute values of one or more existing tuples. DELETE: Used to remove tuples from a relation. 3. Data Control Language (DCL) DCL commands are used to control access to data within the database. They manage user permissions and the integrity of database transactions. The primary DCL commands include: GRANT: Used to pass privileges on database objects to other users. REVOKE: Used to take back (cancel) privileges from users. COMMIT: Used to save transactions permanently. ROLLBACK: Used to undo transactions if an error occurs. Summary SQL is the standard language for interacting with relational databases. It is functionally divided into three core components: DDL (Create, Alter, Drop): Defines and manages the database's structure. DML (Select, Insert, Update, Delete): Manipulates the data stored within that structure. DCL (Grant, Revoke, Commit, Rollback): Controls access and manages transactions. Understanding these three categories is the foundational step to mastering SQL and effectively managing relational databases.
